## Install

Nothing here is code-signed yet, so your system will ask you to confirm the first time.

| | File | First time |
|---|---|---|
| **Windows** | `BoardDock-3.1.1-win-x64-setup.exe` (installer) or `BoardDock-3.1.1-win-x64-portable.exe` (no install) | Choose **More info → Run anyway**. |
| **macOS** (Apple Silicon) | `BoardDock-3.1.1-mac-arm64.dmg` (open it and drag BoardDock into Applications) | Right-click the app and choose **Open**. |
| **Linux** | `BoardDock-3.1.1-linux-x86_64.AppImage` (`chmod +x` it, then run it) or the `.deb` (`sudo apt install ./BoardDock-3.1.1-linux-amd64.deb`) | Nothing. |
| **In your browser** | [danmover.github.io/boarddock](https://danmover.github.io/boarddock) | Nothing is uploaded: it all runs in your browser. |

## What's changed

### Columns of small boards
- **The spring clips between two holders in a column are fine.** Every clip on column holders was measured against its neighbours across 37 column setups. The clips sit in the 6.8 mm gap between two holders, beside the landing, with 5.2 mm of room against the 0.85 mm they need to flex, and their slits print open.
- **No plug points up a column any more.** A board below the top with a plug on its far edge pointed it into the holder above. The plug and its cradle stood where that holder sits, so it sat 3 to 4 mm deep in the one below and its clips were buried. A column's base (a Pico, ESP32, Nano or Sensor board under another board) now stands on a long edge like the rest of its column, with its plugs to the side.
- **A board that can't avoid it is flagged.** A Pi Zero has all its plugs on one long edge, so below the top of a column one always points up. It gets a **Plug up the column** check, which says to put it at the top of its column.

### Documentation
- **The README is 111 lines instead of 722.** It covers what BoardDock is, what the first print showed, downloads, a quick start to a first print, and what it does. The reference moved, corrected, to [docs/](https://github.com/danmover/boarddock/tree/main/docs):
  - the guide to using the app;
  - how the printed parts work, with their checks and FEA;
  - printing;
  - supported files;
  - known limits;
  - development.

## Known limits

Nothing from 3.1 has been printed yet. The fixes from the first print (release button, socket latch, tongue stoppers, spring clips only) come from the model and its checks. See the [3.1.0 notes](https://github.com/danmover/boarddock/releases/tag/v3.1.0) and [docs/limits.md](https://github.com/danmover/boarddock/blob/main/docs/limits.md).
